(I) Main bu siness and product use of the Company
Headquartered in Industry Cluster Area, Jiaozuo, Henan Province, the Company is a large -scale
inorganic fine chemical group mainly engaged in production and sales of titanium dioxide (TiO 2)
pigment , sponge titanium, zirconium products and sulfuric acid, and is also the largest titanium
dioxide pigment manufacturing enterprise in Asia.
Titanium dioxide
The chemical formula for titanium dioxide pigment is TiO 2.
Titanium dioxide pigment is a bright
white pigment with a high refractive index and UV resistance.
It’s excellent light scattering
properties and its high opacity make it a key ingredient in formulations for a wide range of products
worldwide including indoor and outdoor paints, inks, plasti cs, paper, electronics, rubber, fibers,
ceramics, enamels, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and sunscreens.
There are two main types of titanium dioxide pigment, rutile and anatase, also known as pigmentary
titanium dioxide and non -pigmentary titanium dioxide respectively .
Generally, titanium dioxide that
is mainly used in applications such as paints, inks, plastics and paper is referred to as rutile or
pigmentary titanium dioxide , and titanium dioxide that is mainly used for purity in applications
such as fibers, enamel, electric welding rod, ceramics, and electronics, is generally referred to as
anatase or non -pigmentary titanium dioxide .
Titanium sponge
Titanium spong e is typically produced by processing titanium rich ores like ilmenite in a
metallurgical reaction that generate s titanium tetrachloride which is then react ed with magnesium to
generate a sponge -like porous “titanium sponge ”.
Titanium sponge is an important raw material
used to produ ce titanium products like titanium ingots and al loys .
Owing to its low density, high
specific strength, low thermal conductivity, high resistance to high and low temperature s, strong
corrosion resistance and good biocompatibility, titanium metal is widely used in aviation,
aerospace, shipbuilding, weap onry, biomedicine s, chemical metallurgy, marine engineering, sports
& leisure and for a range of other consumer applications.
For this reason, t itanium metal is also
referred to as a “space metal ”, an “ocean metal ”, a “modern metal ” and a “strategic metal ”.
(II) Development status and cyclical characteristics of the industry
Titanium dioxide pigment
The global titanium dioxide pigment industry is almost 100 years old .
It has grown by acquisition
and merger, restructuring and technological advancement.
The titanium dioxide pigment industry in
China began over 60 years ago with the production of enamel and welding electrode titanium
dioxide in 1956.
In the mid -1980s, project ‘ Panzhihua Vanadium -Titanium Magnetite Resources
Comprehensive Utilization ’ improved production equipment and sulfate -process technology to
manufacture rutile titanium dioxide pigments for coatings .
In the 1980s and 1990s, a succession of
titanium dioxide pigment factories were built throughout the country which developed slowly due
to their small production scale, low -tech approach and poor product quality.

titanium dioxide pigment industry has developed rapidly and competes in the international titanium
dioxide p igment market .
Since 2009, with the rapid growth of the Chinese national economy,
market demand for titanium dioxide pigment has been advancing by leaps and bounds, market
prices have risen rapidly, social capital has been continuously attracted, and manufacturers in the
industry have also further expanded successively, leading to a significant increase , from 2011, in the
production capacity of domestic titanium dioxide pigment .
However, at the same time, China ’s GDP
growth rate slowed and the country ’s economic structure changed , especially the demand growth
rate from downstream industries such as real estate and paints, which gradually declined, resulting
in an oversupply of ordinary anatase and rutile products in the industry and a continuous decline in
market prices.
In 2016, under the impetus of a series of policy measures such as the national supply -side structural
reform, “de -capacity, destocking, deleveraging, cost reduction, improving weak links, stable
growth, quality and efficiency improvement, innovation -driven development and transformational
development ”, China ’s titanium industry gradually improved and was rejuvenated .
Since 2016, the
market for titanium dioxide pigment products has boomed, leading to an upward trend in product
prices, tight supplies, great reduction in stocks and year -by -year growth in annual export volume.
present, China ’s titanium dioxide pigment industry is transformi ng.
G rowth in the production of
titanium dioxide pigment using the chloride process, steady improvement in product quality, and
breakthroughs made in technological process es is narrowing the gap with international titanium
dioxide pigment manufacturing giants .
T he spotlight is now on the advantages that circular
econom y manufacturing will bring to China ’s titanium dioxide industry .
Titanium dioxide pigment
producers in China whose focus is on manufacturi ng excellence have invested to buil d unique
circular economy manufacturing chain s, based on the local conditions in whic h they operate .
whole, the “quantity ” of industrial development has been effectively controlled and the “quality ” is
constantly improving.
And China is gradually developing from a large titanium dioxide pigment
manufacturing country to a titanium dioxide pigment manufacturing superpower.
Titanium sponge
In the mid -1950s, the titanium industry and China began research and development into the
production of titanium and titanium alloys , followed, in the early 1960s by the pro duction of semi -
industrial titanium and in the mid -1960s, mass production of titanium sponge and titanium
materials.
Demand for titanium in China has been on the rise since 2008.
It reached a peak in
2011 after which domestic demand for titanium began to de cline and China’s titanium industry
showed structural overcapacity.
However, s ince 2017, d riven by demand from high -end chemical,
aerospace, shipbuilding, power and other industries, demand for titanium processing materials in
China has reached record levels , lea ding to a new high demand for titanium sponge.
In the past decade or so, driven by the rapid growth of the national economy , China ’s titanium
industry has grown further .
China now ranks first in the world for the production of ti tanium sponge
and processed titanium materials .
Currently, high -end aviation titanium materials are in short
supply, there is over -supply of some medium and low -end titanium materials .

(IV) The u pstream and downstream industrial manufacturing chain operated by Lomon
Billions to produce its main products
There are two different branches to the industrial manufacturing chain operated by the Company to
produce its main products .
The first branch concerns the production of titanium dioxide pigment , beginning with the mining
and treatment of ilmenite and rutile ores , followed by the manufactur e, using chemical processes, of
the chemical intermediate p roduct titanium dioxide pigment which is used in the coating s, plastic s,
inks, papermaking and other industries :
mining and treatment of ilmenite and rutile ores – manufacturing of titanium concentrate –
manufacturing of titanium dioxide pigment.
The second branch concerns the production of titanium sponge, beginning with the mining and
treatment of ilmenite and rutile ores , followed by the manufactur e of titanium sponge which is used
to make various metal products used in aerospace and other industries :
mining and treatment of ilmenite and rutile ores – manufacturing of titanium concentrate –
manufacturing of titanium -rich slag – manufacturing of titanium sponge.

pigm ent was high due to the rise in the price of titanium ore and other raw materials.

Prospects for the Company ’s Future Development
Having experienced ten years of accumulation and advancement under the “Twelfth Five -Year
Plan ” and the “Thirteenth Five -Year Plan ” after it went public in 2011, the Company has developed
into a large chemical enterprise engaged in the in -depth integration of titanium and zirconium
industrial manufacturing chains and the R&D and manufacturing of new materials, as well as
becoming the largest titanium dioxide pigment enterprise in Asia.
The Company is one of the few
enterprises in the global titanium dioxide pigment industry that has two production processes for
manufacturing titanium dioxide pigment , i.e. the sulfate process and the chloride process , and
whose business operations cover the entire industr ial manufacturing chain, the only enterprise in
China that possesses titanium dioxide production technology using the large -scale fluidized chloride
process , and also the only enterprise in the industry that possesses two production processes for
manufacturing chlori de titanium dioxide pigment , i.e. the molten salt chloride process and the
fluidized chloride pr ocess .
The Company has the largest -scale direct -current furnace process and
alternating -current furnace process in China for titanium slag production and is the only enterprise Full Text of 2020 Annual Report of Lomon Billions Group Co., Ltd.
in the world that has both the “dry ” and “wet ” processes for chloride titanium dioxide pigment
production.
In addition, the Company has located the chloride process and the sulfate process in one
production area and brought about the first -ever “sulfur -chlorination coupling ” process to achieve
comprehensive resource utilizat ion and comprehensive energy saving and cost reduction, which has
set a precedent in the industry, and also has deployed the entire industrial manufacturing chain
covering titanium ore, high -titanium slag, chlorinated titanium dioxide and titanium sponge i n one
production area to achieve low -cost co -production and process coupling in a larger scale and to a
larger extent.
Through strategic exploration in to “sulfur -chlori de coupling technology ”, the
Company has set a role model in the global titanium dioxide pigment industry in terms of
production cost control and has thoroughly conquered the “three key challenges ” in the titanium
dioxide pigment industry, especially in production technology usi ng the sulfate process , which can
effectively strengthen the Company ’s dominant position in global competition and cooperation.
far, in the titanium industry, the Company has seven production site in six locations in five
provinces in China , namely Jiao zuo in Henan Province, Deyang and Panzhihua in Sichuan
Province, Xiangyang in Hubei Province, Chuxiong in Yunnan Province and Jinchang in Gansu
Province, forming a full -industrial manufacturing chain ranging from mining and dressing of
vanadium titano -magn etite, intensive processing of such raw materials as reduced titanium,
titanium -rich slag and synthetic rutile, to the production of sulfate titanium dioxide pigment ,
chlor ide titanium dioxide pigment and titanium sponge .

Development trends of the industry in whic h the Company conducts business operations
The titanium dioxide pigment industry is a niche industry.
Overall enhancement has been made in
scale and quality of this industry in China since it has been experiencing rapid development for over
In recent years, the titanium dioxide pigment industry has gradually entered a new normal,
evolving from high -speed growth to medium -low -speed growth, with the product structure having
been upgraded from middle and low end to middle and high end.
Under the pressure of supply -side
reform and environmental protection policies, green , energy -saving and environmental protection
have become the mainstream of the industry ’s development.
Recycling economy and producing
titanium dioxide pigment using the chloride process are where the industry is headed, and
development with high quality h as become the main melody of the industry.
Owing to its low density, high intensity, low thermal conductivity, high resistance to high and low
temperature s, strong corrosion resistance and good biocompatibility, titanium is widely used in
aviation, aerospa ce, biomedicine s, chemical metallurgy, marine engineering and other fields, and
therefore titanium is also known as a “space metal ”, an “ocean metal ”, a “modern metal ” and a
“strategic metal ”.
As a fundamental industry for national economic development and industrial
upgrading as well as a key industry supported and prioritized by the state, the titanium industry is of
strategic value to the development of national defense, economy, and science and technology of a
In view of this, China has introdu ced a series of policies to support the development of this
Demand for titanium in China has been on the rise since 2008.
After the titanium material
market reached a peak in 2011, domestic demand for titanium began to decline and China ’s titanium Full Text of 2020 Annual Report of Lomon Billions Group Co., Ltd.
industry showed structural overcapacity.
Currently, t he supply of high -end aviation titanium
materials is in short supply, and the production capacity of civil medium and low -end titanium
materials is seriously oversupplied.
China ’s demand for t itanium processing materials has reached a
record high since 2017, driven by demand from high -end chemical, aerospace, shipping and power
industries.

From the perspective of the structure of downstream applications, lithium -ion batteries are
mainly classified into three types ; energy storage batteries, consume r batteries and power batteries.
Lithium -ion batteries available in the global market are mainly batteries used in electric vehicles
and consumer batteries.
According to the data from www.gg -lb.com, the demand for power lithium
batteries, consumer lithium batteries, energy storage batteries and batteries for other applications
(such as for power tools and electric vehicles) accounted for 46.7%, 40.0%, 5.1% and 8.2%

In view of the fact that the new energy vehicle industry prospers in Ch ina,

The Company will build a low -cost co -produ ction system covering the production of titanium

sponge and high -end titanium alloys by focusing on its existing key resources and advantages, and
will further optimize its green and greater -circulation industrial manufacturing chain to build a
complete industrial manufacturing chain integrating mining and processing of titanium ore, titanium
dioxide pigment production by the chloride process , titanium sponge production, titanium metals
production and processing of titanium materials.
Based on the concept of resource recycling and
green development, the Company will make active efforts to expand its bu siness operations in the
fields of vanadium, zirconium, iron, scandium, cobalt and other titanium derivatives and in the
emerging industries such as intelligent manufacturing and new energy materials and make
continuous efforts to enhance the coupling and integration of its business segments.
will attach importance to both “project construction ” and “M&A and reorganization ”, form a “green
and high -quality titanium industry manufacturing chain ” in alignment with market and industry
development tr ends , carry out resource planning and development layout through M&As in the
capital market and project construction, and ultimately build a green and greater -circulation
industrial manufacturing system.

effectively enhance its main raw material self -sufficiency rate and the multipurpose utilization rate
of mineral resources, ensure the green, safe, stable and reliable supply of raw materials, and provide
guarantee for building a low -cost and full process titanium industry chain.

conduct technological transformation and scale expansion of existing mining areas, reinforce
management excellenc e, and increase recovery rate, production efficiency and output; accelerate the Full Text of 2020 Annual Report of Lomon Billions Group Co., Ltd.
construction and put into operation the innovative project of upgrading and converting 500,000 -
ton ne Panxi titanium concentrates into chlorinated titanium slag to realize mass production of
chlorinated titanium slag upgraded and converted from titanium concentrates produced in China ,
and to enhance the comprehensive utilization value of mineral resources; seek and acquire high -
quality titanium ore at home and abroad to ensure su stainable self -sufficiency in titanium ore.
Enrich product structure and improve product quality
In the titanium dioxide pigment industry : The Company will become a pioneer in industrial
reform of the titanium dioxide pigment industry in China by inc reasing the proportion of chlori de

construction of its 200,000 -ton ne chlori de titanium dioxide production capacity at Chuxiong ,
develop workable subsequent production capacity plans and accelerate business expansion, so as to
seize the great development opportunities in chlori de titanium dioxide pigment production in China

develop new and high -end products with excellent light reflectance and weather resistance,

and localized network for marketing to provide differentiated products and services in areas
designated in the world as per the demands of customers and end -use product formulations ; (2)
build Lomon Billions Shanghai Market Service Center, make the best use of talent, technology,
finance, polic ies and other resources in the Yangtze River Delta and take into account both domestic
and foreign markets to enhance its status and brand advantages in titanium and titanium derivative
related industries; (3) make an appropriate production plan s for titan ium dioxide pigment s produced
by the sulfate process and the chloride process , titanium sponge and high -end titanium alloys, and
conduct business expansion in the fields of vanadium, zirconium, iron, scandium, cobalt and other
titanium derivatives and in emerging industries such as intelligent manufacturing and new energy Full Text of 2020 Annual Report of Lomon Billions Group Co., Ltd.
materials ; (4) pay close attention to the industry ’s mainstream customers, gain insight into customer
demands, keep ing an eye on the competitor and industry developments , and make use of its
advantages in terms of innovation to seize the market.
Green, recyclabl e and sustainable development
The Company will increase its innovation input and upgrade its existing technologies to realize
multipurpose utilization of waste water and solid resources.
The Company will: (1) upgrade and
improve and optimize the existing s ulfuric acid production process, and realize the harmony
between titanium dioxide pigment production and environmental protection; (2) accelerate the
horizontal coupling and integration of the sulfate process and the chloride process , build a synthetic
rutile production line, and ensure the source of the raw materials used in producing titanium dioxide
pigment by the chloride process ; (2) explore multiple applications of ferrous sulfate, and further
reduce the output of solid waste titanium gyp sum; (3) facilitate the coupling between the processes,
and reduce water consumption; (4) separate and recycle the ore and coke in inert waste residues
through the comprehensive utilization project of chlorinated inert waste residues, and increase the
recy cling rate of raw titanium materials.
(IV) Possible risks and countermeasures
Environmental policy related risks
The developing political environment requires enterprises to achieve green development.
national environmental standards, resource re cycling standards and production safety standards will
push for the adopt ion of the international standard s of the world’s developed countries and leading
companies and will promote the strengthen ing of law enforcement.
With higher standards, stricter
requirements and continuous strengthening of environmental supervision, chemical companies will
face environmental risks in the next few years.
Responses: The Company always attaches great importance to ful filling environmental protection
and social responsibility , firmly establishes the concept of ecological priority and green
development, takes the initiative to comply with new standards and new requirements for the
treatment of waste water, waste gas, dus t, noise and solid waste, and continuously increase s its
investment in environmental protection to ensure normal operation of environmental protection
facilities and standard -compliant discharge of various pollutants.
At the same time, the Company, in
acco rdance with the principle of “reduction, reuse and recycling ”, relies on technological
advancement and technological innovation to vigorously develop comprehensive utilization and a
circular economy.
Operation and management related risks
During this re porting period, the Company has experienced rapid development and has formed a
trans -regional group management mode l based on its seven production sites , resulting in the
requirement for increased management abilities.
In view of the increasingly complex and volatile
macroeconomic environment, any inability of the Company to continue to improve the level of its
management abilities and its decision -making efficiency may have a certain impact on the
Company ’s normal prod uction and operation.
Responses: The Company will take into account its development strategy outline d for the next ten
years and its “Fourteenth Five -Year ” Development Plan to unify its management philosophy and
development goals, always maintain a new and innovative way of thinking, continuously improve
the knowledge structure of the Company ’s employees by continuing to improve the level of its
operation s and management abilities through multi -level and multi -channel training and
communication, and actively recruit relevant industry talent and management teams.
Risks in raw material price fluctuation Full Text of 2020 Annual Report of Lomon Billions Group Co., Ltd.
In view of the fact that ever -changing policy factors a nd complex market environment s will lead to
more frequent price fluctuation s in bulk raw materials and will have a greater impact on the
production and operation and cost control of enterprises, the Company will inevitably bear the risk
of fluctuations in raw material prices.
Responses: Build a more perfect industrial manufacturing chain through domestic and foreign
resource integration and technological innovation to achieve the goal of industrial integration as
soon as possible; cooperate with upstream su ppliers to further expand the mining and mineral
separation capabilities of Group companies, strive to grasp the market trend, make profits,
appropriately avoid risks in raw material price fluctuations, and ensure the stability of production
and operation.
Investment risks
In order to realize the strategic structure of the Company ’s titanium industry as soon as possible, the
Company will continue to carry out domestic and overseas industrial mergers and acquisitions as
well as resource integration based on its main business.
There is investment risk since investment in
each project will be affected by various factors such as domestic and international economic
environment s, macro policies, industry cycle s and trading plan s.
Responses: In order to effectiv ely resolve the investment risks associated with industrial mergers
and acquisitions, the Company will engage professional project teams to carry out investment
related cooperation in carefully select ed investment targets, carry out comprehensive project d ue
diligence, establish an efficient investment decision -making mechanism, fully pay attention to ,
prevent , and strictly control risk.
Exchange rate risks
As the largest export enterprise of titanium dioxide pigment in China, the annual export volume of
the Company accounts for 30% -40% of China ’s export volume of titanium dioxide pigment , with
the potential of continuous growth.
As the Company grows its international business , its import and
export business will gradually increase, and any exchange rate fluctuation may result in exchange
loss risks.
Responses: Improve the level of financial and foreign exchange business expertise in relevant
management personnel, actively pay attention to the fluctuations of the foreign exchange market
and e xchange rate trends, enhance market prediction abilit ies , and seek advantages and avoid risks.
Actively make use of advanced financial instruments, flexibly make adjustments to policies
concerning export settlement and pricing and avoid the risks that may result from exchange rate
fluctuations to the maximum extent.
COVID -19 and other ‘black swan ’ (unpredictable) events
In 2020, COVID -19 hit the whole world without warning , and governments around the world have
taken prompt countermeasures.
The epidemic, although having been brought under control, is likely
to return , exposing the Company to uncertainties in procurement, logistics, production and
marketing.
Response measures: The Company will keep a close eye on the epidemic, take stringent actions for
ep idemic prevention and control, adopt active and flexible response measures in line with market
changes, and make continuous efforts to reduce costs while expanding domestic and foreign
marketing activities, so as to ensure stable growth in the Company ’s bu siness performance.
addition, the Company will, on the basis of the concept of being innovation -driven, continue to
optimize its product structure, enrich its product categories, flexibly adjust its production and sales
strategies, take more proactive r esponse measures against ‘black swan ’ events, seize opportunities
in the face of challenges, and revitalize the titanium industry.

Overview of Social Responsibility
Performance of social responsibility
In 2020, adhering to the strategy of “Driven by Project ”, Lomon Billions Group : paid taxes in good
faith, ab ide d by laws and regulations, consciously fulfilled corporate responsibilities, attached great
value to the care of people , took concrete actions for poverty alleviation, was actively in volved in
social ly responsib le construction, supported vigorously and provided funds for village -enterprise
joint construction , provided poverty alleviation through education, industrial poverty alleviation,
‘ecological civilization ’ construction and socia l welfare, and made positive contributions to rural
revitalization and the poverty alleviation cause nationwide.
With regard to village -enterprise joint
construction, the Company invested a total of more than RMB2.513 billion into rural revitalization
and poverty alleviation projects.
For example, Panzhihua Company donated RMB1.121 million for
local infrastructure construction and industrial development, including installation of street lights
for Halang Village and Rilong Village in Muli County, road impro vements and construction of
access roads and bridges in Miyi County and Yanbian County, purchase of baby chicks in Hongyan
Village and Zhuangfang Village in Miyi County, and funding for poor households in Xiaojiaping
Village , I n industrial development; Dey ang Company donated RMB1.145 million to fund the
village -enterprise joint construction project of Xinshi Town Government, construction of waste
transfer stations for Baimiao Village and the party member activity center construction project of
Huoshi Villag e; Xiaoyang Company invested RMB90,000, of which RMB30,000 was used to buy a
garbage truck for Chejiadian Village and RMB60,000 was donated to Xiaoyan Xinghuaping Village
(an object of targeted poverty alleviation); Xinli Company donated RMB157,000 to fund new
countryside construction in Yangjie Village.
With regard to poverty alleviation through education,
the Company invested a total of more than RMB123,600 to fund education and poverty alleviation
activities such as Jiaozuo Love, Childr en ’s Day Charity and Charity for Extremely Poor Students,
and in particular, the Company donated RMB100,000 to Qinfeng Town, Lufeng County, Chuxiong
Prefecture; with regard to ‘ecological civilization ’ construction, the Company played a leading role
in lan dscap e improvements and fulfilled the responsibility of ecological environmental protection
by donating a total of more than RMB25.8 million to fund plant environmental renovation, slag
yard landscaping , woodland improvement s, plant and surrounding environ ment landscape
improvements , and unique green landscape building; with regard to social welfare, the Company

Remuneration policies
(I) General remuneration provisions
The Company adheres to the remuneration principle of “post -based, performance -based and
ability -based remuneration ”, and attaches great importance to value creation, value evaluation and Full Text of 2020 Annual Report of Lomon Billions Group Co., Ltd.
value di stribution.
The Company takes ability and performance as the most fundamental criteria for
evaluating employee value and determines remuneration structure based on post characteristics,
employee capabilities and job performance, and has established a value distribution system focusing
on matching between employee contributions and remuneration.
Basic principles
Based on the basic principles of external competitiveness, internal fairness, employee incentives,
corporate profitability and social legitimacy, the Company ensures the competitiveness of its
remuneration standards, fairly evaluates the value created by employees to it, determines
remuneration based on employees ’ work performance and according to national and local labor and
personnel policies and regulations, and pays due taxes according to law.
Employees ’ total remuneration is composed of base salary, individual bonus, allowances and
subsidies, year -end bonus and other amounts.
(II) Remuneration evaluation
The Company conducts employee remuneration assessment by using the monthly performance
assessment method in terms of actual monthly income -output accomplishment rate, department
performance, job responsibilities, comprehensive quality and other aspects.
The Company conducts monthly evaluation on its subsidiaries in accordance with the annual
performance evaluation program or the economic liability contract, mainly covering monthly
production and business results of each subsidiary in terms of output, quality, cost, safety an d
environmental protection of products.
(III) Employee benefits
Employees being on duty and offering labor services as required are entitled to various social
insurance funds and housing provident fund according to applicable national regulations and th e
Company ’s policies.
Each employee is entitled to seniority allowance as per his/her length of service in the Company.
Employees being on duty as required every month are entitled to meal, medical, travel and other
subsidies.
In 2020, the Company br ought about comprehensive reform of its remuneration and welfare system,
thoroughly improved remuneration and benefits of employees, and established a sound
remuneration and welfare system to allow employees to benefit from its profits and to enhance
emplo yees ’ sense of belonging, belief and happiness.
The Company will strive to achieve a better
situation in which “the Company functions well and employees live in harmony ” with more
competitive remunerations and benefits, more human -oriented welfare mechanis m and more
scientific management.

The Company is fully independent from its controlling shareholder in terms of business, personnel,
assets, organization, finance and other aspects, and has independent and integrated business
operations as well as independent business capacities.
In terms of business: The Company conducts busin ess independent from its controlling
shareholder and subsidiaries without relying on any shareholder or other affiliate and has an
independent and comprehensive supply -production -marketing system.
In terms of personnel: The Company is fully independent from any other individual or entity in
terms of personnel, labor service, human resources and payroll.
Presidents, Vice Presidents,
Financial Officers and other senior executives of the Company serve and get paid by the Company,
and do not serve and get pa id by the Company ’s controlling shareholder and its subsidiaries.
In terms of assets: The Company has production and business premises independent of its
controlling shareholder, an independent and complete asset structure, independent production
system , auxiliary production system and supporting facilities, land use rights, housing titles and
other assets, and an independent procurement and marketing system.
In terms of organization: The Company has established a sound organizational system and runs
independently without any mixed business operations or shared business premises with its
controlling shareholder and other entities controlled by it.

(II) Goodwill impairment
For accounting policies on goodwill, please refer to Note
III(5)/(19); for disclosure of goodwill, please refer to Note V(18).
On December 31, 2020, book value of goodwill in the
consolidated financial statements of Lomon Billions was RMB6.1

of goodwill.
The above goodwill was mainly formed as a result of
Lomon Billions ’ acquisition of Sichuan Lomon Titanium Industry
Co., Ltd. (now renamed as Longbai Sichuan Titanium Industry
Co., Ltd.) in 2016, Panzhihua Ruierxin Industry and Trade Co.,
Ltd. in 2017, Yunnan Metallurgical Xinli Titanium Co., Ltd. in
2019, and Guangdong Or ient Zirconic Industry Science and
Technology Co., Ltd. in 2020.
The management of the Company conducted impairment test on
goodwill at the end of each year and adjusted book value of
goodwill based on results of the impairment test.
Impairment test
is car ried out based on recoverable amount of the asset group
including goodwill which is determined by the higher of present
value of the estimated future cash flows of the asset group and net
amount of the fair value of the assets after deducting disposal
expe nses.
Forecasting future cash flows involves key assumptions
about forecasted revenue, growth rate and profit margin and
determination of appropriate discount rate.
Since these key
assumptions are inherently uncertain and may be affected by bias
of the man agement, we identify the impairment of goodwill in the
consolidated financial statements as a key audit matter.
Our main audit procedures for the impairment test of goodwill are:
Learning about control procedures of the goodwill impairment
test of Lomon Billions, including the asset groups divided by the
Company and the Company ’s judgment on the value of the asset
Evaluate competency, professionalism and objectivity of
external valuation experts appointed by the management;
Evaluating the methods and assumptions used in estimating the
present value of future cash flows based on the requirements of
accounting standards;
Assessing the appropriateness of parameters such as discount
rate and growth rate in the discounted cash flow model used by
external experts.
Such parameters include the estimated
production, future sales price, growth rate, estimated gross profit
margin and related expenses of the asset group, which may be
compared with historical data and industry levels of relevant a sset
Evaluate whether the disclosure of goodwill impairment in the
financial statements meets the requirements of the Accounting
Standards for Business Enterprises.

CPA ’s Responsibilities in Auditing the Financial Statements
Our objectives are to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements as a whole
are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and to issue an auditor ’s report
that includes our opinion.
Reason able assurance is a high level of assurance but is not a guarantee
that an audit conducted in accordance with the auditing standards will always detect a material
misstatement when it exists.
Misstatements can arise from fraud or error and are considered
material if, individually or in the aggregate, they could reasonably be expected to influence the
economic decisions of users taken on the basis of these financial statements.
As part of an audit in accordance with the auditing standards, we exercise professional judgment
and maintain professional skepticism throughout the audit.
(I) Identify and assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, due to fraud or
error, design and perform audit procedures responsive to those risks, and obtain audit evidence that
is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our opinion.
The risk of not detecting a material
misstatement resulting from fraud is higher than for one resulting from error, as fraud may involve
collu sion, forgery, intentional omissions, misrepresentations, or the override of internal control.
(II) Understand the internal controls related to audit so as to design appropriate audit procedures.
(III) Evaluate the appropriateness of accounting policies us ed and the reasonableness of accounting

(IV) Draw a conclusion on the appropriateness of management ’s use of the going -concern

At the same time, based on the audit evidence obtained, it is possible to draw

Basis of Preparation for Financial Statements
Preparation basis
These financial statements are prepared in accordance with the Enterprise Accounting Standards -
Basic Standards promulgated by the Ministry of Finance and various specific corporate accounting
standards, application guidelines for busine ss accounting standards, corporate accounting standards
interpretation and other relevant provisions (hereinafter collectively referred to as “Accounting
Standards for Business Enterprises ”) and related provisions set out in the Preparation Rules for
Infor mation Disclosure by Companies Offering Securities to the Public No. 15 - General Provisions
on Financial Reports issued by China Securities Regulatory Commission.
Besides, these financial statements are prepared by the Company on the bas is of on -going business.
Significant Accounting Policies and Accounting Estimates
Tips for specific accounting policies and accounting estimates:
The information disclosed below has covered the specific accounting policies and accounting
estimates formu lated by the Company based on its actual production and operation characteristics.
Statement of compliance to Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises
These financial statements are in compliance with the requirements of the Accounting Standards for
Business Enterprises enacted by the Ministry of Finance and give a true and complete view of
consolidated and parent company financial position of the Compan y as of December 31, 2020 as
well as consolidated and parent company business performance and cash flows for the year of 2020.
Accounting period
Every accounting period is from January 1 to December 31.
Operating cycle
The Company ’s operating cycle i s 12 months.
Recording Currency
Renminbi (RMB) is adopted by the Company as its recording currency.
Accounting treatment method for business combination under the same control and not
under the same control
Business combination under common control: The assets and liabilities acquired by the combined
party in business combination shall be measured based on carrying amount of the merged party ’s
assets and liabilities (including goodwill formed by the ultimate controlling party ’s acquisition of
the merged party) in the ultimate controlling party ’s consolidated financial statements on the date of
combination.
The difference between book value of the net assets acquired in merger and book Full Text of 2020 Annual Report of Lomon Billions Group Co., Ltd.
value of the merger consideration paid (or total par value of the shares issued) shall be taken into
account in adjusting equity premium in capital reserve; if the capital reserve is insufficient for
offset, the retained earnings shall be adjusted.
Business combination not under the same control: the combination c ost is equivalent to fair value of
the assets handed over, the liabilities incurred or assumed and the equity securities issued by the
acquirer on the acquisition date to obtain control over the acquiree.
The difference between merger
cost and the share of fair value of the identifiable net assets of the acquiree acquired in the merger
(if the former is higher than the latter) is recognized as goodwill; the difference between merger
cost and fair value of the identifiable net assets of the acquiree obtained in the merger (if the former
is lower than the latter) shall be included in the current profit and loss.
The identifiable assets,
liabilities and contingent liabilities acquired from the acquiree in the merger that meet the
recognition conditions shall be measured at their fair values on the acquisition date.
Direct related expenses incurred for business combination are included in the current profit or loss
when incurred; the transaction costs of issuing equity securities or debt securities for business
combination are included in the initial recognition amount of equity securities or debt securities.
Method for preparing consolidated financial statements
Scope of consolidation
The consolidation scope of the consolidated financial statements shall be de termined on the basis of
control, which includes the Company and all of its subsidiaries.
The term “control ” means the
Company ’s possession of the power in an investee to enjoy variable returns by getting involved in
the investee ’s relevant activities, as well as the Company ’s possession of the ability to influence the
investment return from the investee by exercising its power over the investee.
Consolidation procedures
The Company regards the entire group as an accounting entity and refers to the unified accounting
policies when preparing the consolidated financial statements which reflect overall financial
situation, operating results and cash flow of the Company.
The impacts of internal transactions
between the Company and its subsidiaries and between th e Company ’s subsidiaries shall be offset.
If internal transactions show any impairment losses in relevant assets, such losses shall be fully
recognized.
If the accounting policy or accounting period adopted by subsidiaries is inconsistent
with that adopted by the Company, necessary adjustments should be made according to the
accounting policy or accounting period adopted by the Company when preparing consolidated
financial statements.
Owners ’ equity, current net profit or loss and comprehensive income of th e current period of
subsidiaries shall be separately listed under the owners ’ equity item in consolidated balance sheet,
under the net profit item in consolidated income statement and under the comprehensive income

minority shareholders ’ share of owners ’ equity in subsidiaries at the beginning, which offsets
minority shareholders ’ equity.

Testing method and accounting treatment method for the impairment of financial assets
The Co mpany will, in a single or combined manner, estimate the expected credit loss of financial
assets which are measured at amortized cost and financial assets (debt instruments) and financial
guarantee contracts which are measured at fair value with their cha nges included in other
comprehensive income.
The Company will calculate the probability -weighted prevent value amount of the difference
between the cash flows receivable under contracts and the cash flows expected to be received under
contracts and recogni ze expected credit loss by considering reasonable and grounded information
concerning past events, current conditions and forecasts of future financial situation and by taking
the risk of default as the weight.
If the credit risk of the financial instrumen t has increased significantly after the initial recognition,
the Company shall measure its loss reserve based on the amount equivalent to the expected credit
loss of the financial instrument in its whole existence; if the credit risk of the financial instr ument
has experienced no significant increase after the initial recognition, the Company shall measure its
loss reserve based on the amount equivalent to the expected credit loss of the financial instrument in
the future 12 months.
The increased or reverse d amount of loss reserve resulted thereby shall be
included in current profit and loss as impairment loss or gain.
The Company will determine relative changes in the risk of default of financial instruments during
the expected lifetime and determine whethe r the credit risk of financial instruments has significantly
increased since the initial recognition by comparing the risk of default of such financial instruments
on the balance sheet date with that on the initial recognition date.
Generally, in the event of more
than 30 days overdue, the Company deems that the credit risk of the financial instrument has
increased significantly, unless there is conclusive evidence showing that the credit risk of that
financial instrument has not increased significantly aft er initial recognition.
If the financial instrument shows a lower credit loss risk on the balance sheet date, the Company
deems that the credit risk of that financial instrument has not increased significantly after initial
recognition.
If there is objecti ve evidence showing that credit impairment has occurred to certain financial
assets, the Company will set aside impairment reserve for the financial assets on a single item basis.

Risks Associated with Financial Instruments
The Company faces various financial risks in its business operations: credit risk, market risk and
liquidity risk.
The Company ’s board of directors is fully respons ible for determination of risk
management objectives and policies and assumes ultimate responsibility for risk management
objectives and policies.
However, the board of directors has authorized the Company ’s functional
departments to design and implement p rocedures that can ensure effective implementation of risk
management objectives and policies.
The board of directors reviews effectiveness of the
implemented procedures and rationality of the risk management objectives and policies by means of
the monthly reports submitted by heads of the functional departments.
The Company ’s internal
auditors will also audit risk management policies and procedures and report the findings to audit
committee.
Overall goal of the Company ’s risk management is to develop risk management policies that
minimize risks without overly affecting the Company ’s competitiveness and resilience.
Credit risk refers to the risk of the Company ’s financial losses due to its counterparties ’ failure to
perform contractual obligations.
The Company ’s credit risk mainly arises from monetary funds, notes receivable, accounts
receivable, receivables financing, other receivables, debt investments, other debt investments and
financial guarantee cont racts, and also from debt instrument investments and derivative financial
assets that are not included in the scope of impairment assessment and are measured at fair value
with their changes being included in the current profit and loss.
On the balance she et date, book
value of the Company ’s financial assets represented its maximum credit risk exposure.
The Company ’s monetary funds are mainly bank deposits deposited with state -owned banks and
other large and medium -sized listed banks that are in good standing and enjoy high credit ratings.
The Company believes that it is exposed to no major credit risk and will hardl y suffer major losses
due to bank defaults.
In addition, for bills receivable, accounts receivable, receivables financing and other receivables,
the Company have related policies in place to control credit risk exposure.
The Company assesses
the credit qua lification of customers and set corresponding credit period for them on the basis of
their financial status, possibility of obtaining guarantee from third party, credit records and other
factors such as the current market conditions.
The Company will regul arly monitor the credit
records of customers, and for those with adverse credit records, the Company will send them
written notice of a call, and shorten or cancel their credit periods, to ensure the overall credit risk of
the Company under control.

Liq uidity risk
Liquidity risk refers to the risk of a shortage of funds when an enterprise fulfills its obligation to
settle cash or other financial assets.
The Company ’s policy is to ensure that there is sufficient cash to pay off debts as they fall due.
Liq uidity risk is centrally monitored by Finance Department of the Company.
Finance Department
ensures that the Company has sufficient funds to repay debts under all reasonable forecasts by
monitoring cash balances, marketable securities at any time, and rolling forecasts of future 12 -
month cash flows.
Finance Department has also monitored the compliance with loan agreement to
obtain the commitments from major financial institutions to provide adequate reserve fund to meet
short - and long -term fund demands .

The market risk of financial instruments means the risk that the fair value or future cash flow of a
financial instrument fluctuates because of change in the market price, including exchange rate risk,
interest rate risk and other price risks.
Interest rate risk
Interest rate risk means the risk that the fair value or future cash flow of a financial instrument
fluctuates because of change in the market interest rate.
Interest -bearing financial instruments with fixed interest rates and floating interest rates expose the
Company to fair value interest rate risk and cash flow interest rate risk.
The Company determi nes
the proportions of fixed interest rate instruments and floating interest rate instruments based on the
market environment and maintains an appropriate portfolio of fixed and floating interest rate
instruments through regular review and monitoring.
When necessary, the Company will use interest
rate swap instruments to hedge interest rate risk.
Exchange rate risks
Exchange rate risk means the risk that the fair value or future cash flow of a financial instrument
fluctuates because of change in the foreign exchange rate.
The Company constantly monitors foreign currency transactions and size of foreign currency assets
and liabilities to mi nimize the exchange rate risks.
In addition, the Company may also sign forward
foreign exchange contracts or curre ncy swap contracts to avoid exchange rate risk.

Implementation by the Company ’s subsidiary Orient Zirconic Industry of the Restricted
Stock Incentive Plan
The 16th meeting of the 7th Board of Directors of the Company ’s subsidiary Orient Zirconic
Industry that was held on January 25, 2021 and the 1st extraordinary general meeting in 2021 of the
Company ’s subsidiary Orient Zirconic Industry that was held on February 10, 2021 deliberated and
approved the Proposal on the Company ’s 2021 Restricted Stock Incentive Plan (Revised Draft) and
Its Summary .
Pursu ant to the Proposal, Orient Zirconic Industry planned to grant 70,000,000
restricted RMB common shares (A shares) (of which 66,087,000 shares were granted for the first
time and 3,913,000 shares were reserved) to 418 incentive objects through directional i ssuance at a
par value of RMB1 and at a grant price of RMB2.93/per share.
In accordance with the Proposal on
Granting Restricted Shares to Incentive Objects for the First Time deliberated and approved at the
17th meeting of the 7th Board of Directors held on February 10, 2021, and with the authorization at
the 1st extraordinary general meeting in 2021, the Board of Directors decided to grant 66,087,000
restricted shares to 418 eligible incentive objects on February 10, 2021 which was determined as the
date for granting shares.
As at February 26, 2021, Orient Zirconic Industry received subscription price totaling
RMB191,777,290.00 paid by 406 incentive objects (12 incentive objects waived subscription) for
subscribing for 65,453,000 shares in monetary funds.
Registered capital was increased by
RMB65,453,000.00, and capital reserve – equity premium was increased by RMB126,324,290.00.
Profit distribution

approved the Proposal on Profit Distribution in 2020 .
Pursuant to the Proposal, the Company ’s
dividends distribution in 2020 met the requirements of the Shareholder Return Plan for the Next

decided not to distribute profits in 2020.

2020 Annual General Meeting for consideration.
